title: JavaScript Promises: The Three States
description: A beginner course introducing what a JavaScript Promise is, focusing first on its three states before any consumption syntax.
goal: Understand that a Promise represents an eventual result that moves through pending, fulfilled, and rejected states.

units.title: The Three States of a Promise
units.goal: Explain that a Promise is always in exactly one of three states — pending, fulfilled, or rejected — and that its value is not available until it settles.

teacherBrain.persona: a patient JavaScript mentor who builds intuition before syntax
objectives: Name the three states of a Promise.
Explain that a pending Promise has not settled and holds no result yet.
Distinguish a rejected Promise from a pending one.
guidelines: Use plain language and everyday analogies before any code.
Correct the common state confusions gently.
Give a hint before revealing an explanation.
constraints: Do not teach how to consume a Promise with .then() or .catch() — that is the next unit.
Keep to the three states and settling; do not go into chaining.

knowledgeBaseChunks.title: A Promise has three states
knowledgeBaseChunks.content: A Promise is an object that represents a result that is not ready yet. At any moment it is in exactly one of three states: pending (still working), fulfilled (finished successfully with a value), or rejected (finished with an error). It starts pending and settles once, into either fulfilled or rejected.

knowledgeBaseChunks.title: Pending is not the same as rejected
knowledgeBaseChunks.content: A pending Promise is still running and has not settled, so it has no result yet. A rejected Promise has already settled unsuccessfully with an error reason. Pending means unfinished; rejected means finished but failed. They are different states, so a pending Promise is not a failed one.

questions.prompt: Name the three states a Promise can be in.

hints.text: One state is before it finishes, and two are after.
The two finished states are one success and one failure.

commonMistakes.mistake: Thinking a pending Promise is the same as a rejected one.
commonMistakes.correction: A pending Promise is still working and has not settled, while a rejected Promise has already settled with an error. Pending is not the same as rejected — one is unfinished and the other finished unsuccessfully.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming a pending Promise already holds its result value.
commonMistakes.correction: While a Promise is pending its value is not ready yet, so there is no result to read. The value only becomes available once the Promise settles as fulfilled.

units.title: Consuming a Promise with .then() and .catch()
units.goal: Read a settled Promise's outcome using .then() for success and .catch() for errors.

guidelines: Assume the three states are understood.
constraints: Assume unit 1 (the three states) is done.

knowledgeBaseChunks.title: Reading the outcome
knowledgeBaseChunks.content: Once a Promise settles you read its outcome with handler callbacks: a success handler runs with the fulfilled value, and an error handler runs with the rejection reason.

questions.prompt: Which handler runs when a Promise is fulfilled?

hints.text: It pairs with the fulfilled state.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting the success handler to run when the Promise is rejected.
commonMistakes.correction: The success handler only runs on fulfillment; a rejection is handled by the error handler instead.
